question:
The following sentence contains an error. Select the option that correctly rectifies the error.

If I was a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. If I were a king,.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence expresses an unreal / imaginary condition (a wish contrary to fact). In the second/third conditional, the verb "be" takes the subjunctive form "were" for all subjects — so "If I were a king", not "If I was a king".

◦ Correct: If I were a king, I would have tried my best to remove poverty from my country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "on my country" (should be "from my country") is already correct in the sentence; "my best by remove poverty" and "I would has tried" are wrong distractors.

• With "would have + V3", the "if" clause needs the past subjunctive "were".

NOTE

• The subjunctive mood uses "were" for hypothetical/unreal ideas: "If I were you", "I wish I were rich", "As if he were a genius". (काल्पनिक स्थिति में 'were')

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The manager decided to disclose a secret and address the issue at the team meeting.
option_3: hit the nail on the head
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. spill the beans.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "spill the beans" means to reveal/disclose a secret (often unintentionally). It fits "disclose a secret". (राज़ खोल देना)

◦ Correct: The manager decided to spill the beans and address the issue at the team meeting.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "bury the hatchet" = to make peace / end a quarrel.

• Option 3 "hit the nail on the head" = to describe exactly what is causing a situation.

• Option 4 "sweep it under the rug" = to hide/ignore a problem.

NOTE

• Similar idioms of revealing: "let the cat out of the bag", "give the game away", "blow the whistle".

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The blanket gifted by my granny is softer and cozy.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. soft.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adjective "cozy" (positive degree) is joined by "and" to the first adjective, so both must be in the same degree. Since "cozy" is positive, the first should also be positive — "soft", giving "soft and cozy".

◦ Correct: The blanket gifted by my granny is soft and cozy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "softer" (comparative) needs "than" and cannot be paired with the positive "cozy".

• "more soft" is a wrong double form; "softly" is an adverb; "softest" is superlative (needs "the").

NOTE

• When two adjectives describe one noun and are joined by "and", keep them parallel in degree: soft and cozy / softer and cozier / softest and coziest. (समान डिग्री)

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

They was / celebrating their / Silver wedding anniversary / next month in Dubai.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. They was.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject "They" is plural, so it takes the plural verb "were", not the singular "was". So it should be "They were celebrating".

◦ Correct: They were celebrating their Silver wedding anniversary next month in Dubai.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "celebrating their", "Silver wedding anniversary" and "next month in Dubai" are all grammatically correct.

• "were celebrating" (past continuous) also works with a future arrangement here.

NOTE

• Subject–verb agreement: I/He/She/It → was; We/You/They → were. (कर्ता-क्रिया मेल)

question:
Select the word that has the same meaning (SYNONYM) as the underlined word in the given sentence.

Almost as wide as he was tall, he had a voracious appetite for food and drink and a rollicking personality to match.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. insatiable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Voracious" means having a very great appetite; extremely eager/greedy for food (or something). Its closest synonym is "insatiable" (impossible to satisfy). (अतृप्त / भूखा)

◦ Example: He had a voracious/insatiable appetite for food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "vehement" (showing strong feeling), Option 2 "imminent" (about to happen) and Option 4 "venerable" (deserving respect due to age) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of voracious: insatiable, ravenous, greedy, gluttonous, avid. Antonyms: satisfied, moderate. "A voracious reader" = one who reads a great deal.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The police informed the statesman that the goons were up to something mischievious.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. mischievous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "mischievous" (mis-chie-vous), meaning causing or intending to cause trouble/harm in a playful way. (शरारती)

◦ Spelling key: MIS + CHIE + VOUS (no extra "i" after "v").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "mischievious", "mischevious", "mischeivous" and "mischevous" are all common misspellings.

NOTE

• Word family: mischief (noun), mischievous (adjective), mischievously (adverb). Note the "ie" in mischief and mischievous. (वर्तनी)

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The unexpected guest at the party was a bull in a China shop.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. careless and damaging.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a bull in a china shop" describes a clumsy, careless person who causes damage or handles a delicate situation roughly. So it means "careless and damaging". (अनाड़ी / फूहड़)

◦ Correct sense: The unexpected guest was careless and damaging.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "influential and meticulous", Option 3 "careful and compassionate" and Option 4 "leisurely and relaxed" are the opposite of the idiom's meaning.

NOTE

• A "bull in a china shop" acts without care in a place needing gentleness. Related idea: "like a wrecking ball" — causing destruction.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

By next summer, they will be _____ their house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. renovating.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After "will be", the present participle (V-ing) is required to form the future continuous tense. So "will be renovating". (भविष्य सतत काल)

◦ Correct: By next summer, they will be renovating their house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "renovates" (present simple), "renovate" (base form) and "renovated" (past/participle) do not fit after "will be" in an active continuous structure.

NOTE

• Future continuous = will be + V-ing (will be working, will be travelling). It shows an action in progress at a future time. (will be + V-ing)

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

She treats her juniors _____ contempt.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. with.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct collocation is "treat someone with contempt" — the preposition "with" is used to show the manner/attitude. (तिरस्कार के साथ)

◦ Correct: She treats her juniors with contempt.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "by", "in" and "for" are not used with "treat ... contempt".

• "With" commonly follows "treat" to describe attitude: treat with respect/kindness/care/contempt.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: "treat with respect", "look upon with contempt", "hold in contempt", "beneath contempt".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Oppertunity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Oppertunity" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Opportunity", meaning a favourable chance or occasion. (अवसर)

◦ Spelling key: OP + POR + TU + NI + TY (with "or", not "er").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Appearance", "Immigration" and "Astronaut" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Remember: opportunity (double "p", "or" in the middle). Related word: "opportune" (well-timed). (वर्तनी)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Chaotic
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Systematic.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Chaotic" means in a state of complete disorder and confusion. Its antonym is "systematic", meaning done according to an organised plan or method. (अव्यवस्थित का विलोम — व्यवस्थित)

◦ Example: The chaotic office became systematic after the new manager arrived.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Confused" is a synonym of chaotic.

• Options 2 "Dressed" and 3 "Obscure" (unclear) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of chaotic: disordered, confused, disorganised, turbulent. Antonyms: systematic, orderly, organised, methodical.

question:
The given sentence has an error. Select the option that rectifies the error.

The students were asked to turn up their assignments by Friday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. turn in their assignments.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "turn in" means to submit/hand in (work), which is the intended meaning. "Turn up" means "to appear/arrive" or "to increase", which does not fit here. So it should be "turn in their assignments".

◦ Correct: The students were asked to turn in their assignments by Friday.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "The students were asked to" and "their assignments by Friday" are already correct.

• "turn up" (arrive/appear) changes the meaning entirely.

NOTE

• Phrasal verbs with "turn": turn in (submit / go to bed), turn up (appear), turn down (reject), turn over (hand over / flip). (submit = turn in)

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Out of spirits
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Gloomy.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "out of spirits" means feeling low, sad, depressed or gloomy. (उदास / निराश)

◦ Example: He has been out of spirits since he failed the exam — i.e., gloomy.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Cheerful" is the opposite.

• Options 3 "Hurt" and 4 "Obsolete" (outdated) do not match.

NOTE

• Contrast: "in high spirits" = cheerful and lively; "out of spirits / low-spirited" = sad and gloomy.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Illuminate' from the given sentence.

The toughest and most typical question in the examination was to elucidate a particular theory related to friction in physics.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Elucidate.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Illuminate" (in the sense of making something clear) means to explain / throw light on / clarify. Its synonym in the sentence is "elucidate", which means to make something clear by explaining it. (स्पष्ट करना)

◦ Example: The teacher tried to illuminate/elucidate the difficult theory.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Typical" (representative), Option 3 "Particular" (specific) and Option 4 "Theory" (an idea/principle) are not synonyms of "illuminate".

NOTE

• Synonyms of illuminate/elucidate: explain, clarify, clear up, throw light on, expound. Antonyms: obscure, confuse.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.

Everyone in the room was in a jolly and relaxed mood.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No substitution required.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is already grammatically correct. "in a jolly and relaxed mood" uses the positive adjective "jolly" correctly, parallel with "relaxed". No comparative or superlative is needed. So "No substitution required".

◦ Correct: Everyone in the room was in a jolly and relaxed mood.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "most jolly" (superlative) and "jollier" (comparative) would break the positive-degree parallel with "relaxed".

• "more jollier" is a wrong double comparative.

NOTE

• Never combine "more" with the "-er" comparative form ("more jollier" is incorrect). Positive adjectives pair with positive: "jolly and relaxed".

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined word in the given sentence.

Urban people have a bombastic lifestyle, which is very different from those of rural folks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pretentious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bombastic" means high-sounding, showy and pompous; using inflated language or an ostentatious/pretentious manner. So its meaning here is "pretentious". (आडंबरपूर्ण / दिखावटी)

◦ Example: His bombastic/pretentious speech was full of grand but empty words.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Hollow" (empty), Option 3 "Delusive" (deceptive) and Option 4 "Common" (ordinary) do not correctly define bombastic.

NOTE

• Synonyms of bombastic: pretentious, pompous, grandiose, ostentatious, flamboyant. Antonyms: modest, simple, unpretentious.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Occassion.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Occassion" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Occasion" (double "c", single "s"), meaning a particular event or a special/important time. (अवसर)

◦ Spelling key: OC + CA + SION.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Efficient", "Boundary" and "Illustration" are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Remember: occasion has double "c" and single "s". Related: occasional, occasionally. (वर्तनी)

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The new employee is really trying to fit in, but sometimes he feels out of place and uncomfortable.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. a fish out of water.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "a fish out of water" means a person who feels uncomfortable/out of place in an unfamiliar situation or environment. It fits "out of place and uncomfortable". (असहज / बेगाना महसूस करना)

◦ Correct: The new employee sometimes feels like a fish out of water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "a diamond in the rough" = a person with hidden good qualities.

• Option 2 "a bird of a feather" = people of similar type ("birds of a feather flock together").

• Option 4 "a needle in a haystack" = something very hard to find.

NOTE

• "A fish out of water" stresses discomfort in a new/strange setting. Opposite idea: "in one's element" (comfortable and happy).

question:
Select the word segment from the given options that substitutes the highlighted word segment correctly and completes the sentence meaningfully: -

Each of the participants were given a certificate.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. was given.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject is "Each of the participants". "Each" is a singular word and always takes a singular verb, so "were" is wrong and should be "was given".

◦ Correct: Each of the participants was given a certificate.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "have given"/"are given"/"have been given" are plural or wrong-voice forms that do not agree with the singular subject "each".

• Passive singular: "was given" (a certificate was given to each).

NOTE

• Singular subjects that take a singular verb: each, every, either, neither, one of. "Each of the boys is present." (Each + singular verb)

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Captivity
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Liberty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Captivity" means the state of being imprisoned or confined. Its antonym is "liberty", meaning freedom. (कैद का विलोम — स्वतंत्रता)

◦ Example: After years of captivity, the animals were released to liberty.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "Ethnicity" (belonging to a social group), Option 3 "Entity" (a thing that exists) and Option 4 "Authenticity" (genuineness) are unrelated.

NOTE

• Synonyms of captivity: confinement, imprisonment, bondage, incarceration. Antonyms: liberty, freedom, release, emancipation.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. The government has also __3__ flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment. In recent years, the government has allowed companies to __4__ many of these provisions. Instead of hiring workers on a regular basis, companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is __5__ pressure of work. This is done to reduce the cost of labour for the company. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. attract.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The governments are taking steps to "attract" foreign companies to invest — i.e., to draw them in / persuade them to come. This fits the theme of encouraging foreign investment. (आकर्षित करना)

◦ Correct: ... taking special steps to attract foreign companies to invest in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "fulfil" (to carry out), Option 3 "deplore" (to strongly disapprove) and Option 4 "abhor" (to hate) do not fit the positive sense of drawing investment.

NOTE

• "Attract investment / attract tourists / attract attention" are common collocations. Synonyms: draw, lure, entice. Antonyms: repel, deter.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. The government has also __3__ flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment. In recent years, the government has allowed companies to __4__ many of these provisions. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. set up.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are being "set up" — i.e., established/created. The passage then describes their world-class facilities, confirming they are being newly established. (स्थापित किया जाना)

◦ Correct: Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being set up.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "dismantled" (taken apart) and Option 4 "wound up" (closed down) mean the opposite of establishing.

• Option 3 "obeyed" does not suit "zones".

NOTE

• Phrasal verb "set up" = to establish/start (a business, institution, zone). Antonyms: wind up, close down, dismantle.

solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. allowed.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The government has "allowed" flexibility in the labour laws to attract foreign investment — i.e., permitted/given flexibility. (अनुमति देना)

◦ Correct: The government has also allowed flexibility in the labour laws ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "winked" (closed and opened an eye), Option 3 "invited" and Option 4 "suffered" do not collocate with "flexibility in the labour laws".

NOTE

• "Allow flexibility / allow access / allow time" are natural collocations. Synonyms of allow: permit, grant, let. Antonyms: forbid, prohibit.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. Industrial zones, called Special Economic Zones (SEZs), are being __2__. SEZs have world-class facilities, including electricity, water, roads, transport, storage, recreational, and educational facilities. Companies that set up production units in the SEZs do not have to pay taxes for an initial period of five years. Instead of hiring workers on a regular basis, companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is __5__ pressure of work. This is done to reduce the cost of labour for the company. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ignore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The government has allowed companies to "ignore" many of these provisions — i.e., to disregard/not follow them. The next sentence (hiring workers 'flexibly' instead of on a regular basis) explains that the usual labour provisions are being set aside. (अनदेखा करना)

◦ Correct: ... the government has allowed companies to ignore many of these provisions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "flounder" (to struggle), Option 3 "distort" (to twist) and Option 4 "effect" (to bring about) do not fit "provisions" in this context.

NOTE

• "Ignore rules / ignore provisions / ignore advice" — to pay no attention to. Synonyms: disregard, overlook, neglect. Antonyms: heed, observe, follow.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

In recent years, the central and state governments in India have been taking special steps to __1__ foreign companies to invest in India. However, some foreign companies are not satisfied, and they are demanding more in labour laws, citing the need for greater operational efficiency.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. intense.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods when there is "intense" pressure of work — i.e., great/heavy pressure. This explains the need for extra short-term hiring. (तीव्र / अत्यधिक)

◦ Correct: ... for short periods when there is intense pressure of work.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "inadequate" (not enough), Option 3 "mechanical" and Option 4 "artificial" do not logically describe "pressure of work" here — heavy pressure is what causes extra hiring.

NOTE

• "Intense pressure / intense heat / intense competition" — very strong/extreme. Synonyms: severe, extreme, acute. Antonyms: mild, slight, moderate.
